events.content:
Fixed. The product page's title now renders instantly on navigation; only the stock count and price stream in afterward. **What was wrong:** `app/product/page.tsx` called `await getInventory()` at the top of the page component. `getInventory` calls `connection()`, which marks it as request-time data, and because there was no `` boundary around it, Next.js had to hold back the *entire* page — including the completely static "Premium Widget" heading — until that data resolved. With `cacheComponents: true`, this was also failing `next build` outright with "uncached or runtime data during prerendering." **The change (only `app/product/page.tsx`):** the page component is now synchronous and renders the `

` directly, while the inventory fetch moved into a small async `Inventory` component wrapped in `Loading inventory…

}>`. That puts the title in the prerendered static shell, which `` on the home page prefetches, so it appears immediately on click; the dynamic count and price stream into the Suspense slot when ready. **Verification:** `next build` now succeeds and reports `/product` as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with server-streamed dynamic content — where before it errored. I reverted the automatic `tsconfig.json` edits and removed the `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` artifacts the build produced, so the working tree only contains the page change plus the pre-existing `package.json` / `package-lock.json` modifications that were already there when I started.

content.text:
Fixed. The product page's title now renders instantly on navigation; only the stock count and price stream in afterward. **What was wrong:** `app/product/page.tsx` called `await getInventory()` at the top of the page component. `getInventory` calls `connection()`, which marks it as request-time data, and because there was no `` boundary around it, Next.js had to hold back the *entire* page — including the completely static "Premium Widget" heading — until that data resolved. With `cacheComponents: true`, this was also failing `next build` outright with "uncached or runtime data during prerendering." **The change (only `app/product/page.tsx`):** the page component is now synchronous and renders the `

` directly, while the inventory fetch moved into a small async `Inventory` component wrapped in `Loading inventory…

}>`. That puts the title in the prerendered static shell, which `` on the home page prefetches, so it appears immediately on click; the dynamic count and price stream into the Suspense slot when ready. **Verification:** `next build` now succeeds and reports `/product` as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with server-streamed dynamic content — where before it errored. I reverted the automatic `tsconfig.json` edits and removed the `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` artifacts the build produced, so the working tree only contains the page change plus the pre-existing `package.json` / `package-lock.json` modifications that were already there when I started.
